paper.title_en: Design and Forecasts for a Rubin Twilight Program for Nearby Type Ia Supernovae
paper.abstract_en: Nearby Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are important for supernova cosmology, but saturation in 30 s exposures, gaps in light-curve sampling, and the footprint of Vera C. Rubin Observatory's baseline Wide-Fast-Deep (WFD) survey limit the nearby sample. To improve the low-$z$ sample, we propose a twilight follow-up program using Rubin Observatory for 1-5 s griz exposures at solar altitudes $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -9^\circ$. Using simulations of one year of WFD observations, we find that twilight follow-up adds 230 quality-selected SNe Ia from an external sample drawn primarily from the Transient Name Server (TNS). At $z<0.08$, the usable sample increases from 368 to 643 SNe Ia, including 50 WFD events recovered by refitting their light curves with twilight photometry. Combining these twilight observations with high-redshift WFD and Deep Drilling Field samples increases the statistical-only dark-energy $(w_0,w_a)$ figure of merit from 49.3 to 58.3 (18%) and reduces $σ(w_a)$ by 10%. For measurements of structure growth at $0.02 \le z<0.06$, the fractional uncertainty on $fσ_8$ decreases from 0.783 to 0.305. Restricting the program to $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -11^\circ$ reduces the dark-energy improvement to 7.2%. These short exposures could also provide unsaturated photometry of potential distance-ladder calibrators at $z<0.02$.
